text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- International community will not pour money into Bosnia until there is progress towards a market economy and democracy, U.S. President Clinton's special envoy to Bosnia, Richard Sklar, told the newspaper.
- Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister meets on Tuesday with the U.S. tobacco company Phillip Morris representatives to renew cooperation in Bosnia.

- The Moslem SDA party is the second-strongest party in the Bosnian Serb parliament and is entitled to have its official as the deputy president, Avdo Campara, the secretary of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation parliament said.

- The German company Bosch presents its latest communications equipment in Sarajevo and its experts will hold a series of lectures for Bosnian businessmen in the coming days. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
